questions.q:
Which of the following is/are the example/ examples of chemical change?Crystallization of sodium chloride
2. Melting of ice
3. Souring of milk
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.explain: A change in which one or more new substances are formed is called a chemical change. A chemical change is also called a chemical reaction. Chemical changes are very important in our lives. All new substances are formed as a result of chemical changes. Crystallization is the physical process of solidification of a liquid substance into a highly structured solid whose atoms or molecules are placed in a well-defined 3D crystal lattice. Example: Crystallization of sodium chloride. (Statement 1 is not correct) Melting is a physical process that takes place in the phase transition of a substance from a solid to a liquid. Example: Melting of ice. (Statement 2 is not correct) Souring of milk is a chemical change due to this process, acidification takes place and soured milk is produced. (Statement 3 is correct)

questions.q: Water can dissolve more substances than any other liquid because
options: it is a good conductor of heat
it has high value of specific heat
it is an oxide of hydrogen
questions.explain: Water is called the universal solvent because more substances dissolve in water than in any other chemical. This has to do with the polarity of each water molecule. Water molecules have a polar arrangement of the oxygen and hydrogen atoms where one side (hydrogen) has a positive electrical charge, and the other side (oxygen) has a negative charge. This allows the water molecule to become attracted to many other different types of molecules. The oxygen atom in a water molecule is slightly more electronegative than a hydrogen atom. In other words, the oxygen atom is negatively charged, and the hydrogen atoms are positively charged, making the entire water molecule dipolar in nature.
